thread:
rebecca (Design): quick copy review: the small top-right toast when you stop a Dedicated pool reads `Stop initiated` and a single button `Revert`. multiple folks said it's ambiguous about whether jobs were canceled or just queued to stop. screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/stop-toast-v2.png :eyes:

 tom (Product): yeah this confused me during testing. i clicked Revert and it felt like nothing happened for a few secs. would be good to signal what the action means and the undo window.

 chi (Eng): implementation detail: we immediately begin draining and cancel queued jobs, but we do hold a 30s undo window before finalizing shutdown. so the correct state is "stop in progress" not "stopped".

 rebecca (Design): suggested microcopy options to discuss (aim: short + scannable):
  - "Stop in progress — running jobs will be canceled. [Cancel stop]"
  - "Stopping pool — canceling queued jobs. [Undo]"
  - "Stop scheduled — pool is preparing to shut down. [Cancel stop]"
 which reads best? also thinking about voice/tone: use active verbs and keep button labels action-oriented (Cancel stop vs Undo).

 rachel (QA): prefer first option. button `Cancel stop` feels clearer about saving jobs. add tests: aria-live message shows remaining undo seconds, and keyboard focus behavior when user triggers stop with keyboard.

 tom (Product): tiny nit: "running jobs will be canceled" might alarm users. maybe soften: "running jobs will be canceled if not finished" or show a short link to docs. but that makes toast long. suggestion: single-line toast: "Stop in progress — running jobs may be canceled. [Cancel stop]" with a tooltip or accessible description linking to detail.

 chi (Eng): agree with keeping toast single-line. runtime logs also emit an event with full details we can surface in activity feed. for consistency, other toasts are like `Deploy started` / `Rollback applied` so maybe use `Stop started` or `Stop in progress` to match tense.

 rebecca (Design): new compact copy: `Stop in progress — running jobs may be canceled. [Cancel stop]` and i'll add `role=alert` and an `aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden element with expanded text: "The pool is draining. Running jobs will be canceled immediately. You have 30 seconds to cancel the stop."

 rachel (QA): add test cases: 1) toast copy during network failover; 2) ensure `Cancel stop` call is idempotent; 3) screen reader reads expanded description on show.

 helper-bot: branch "toast-stop-copy-fix" created -> PR #853

 rebecca (Design): great, i'll update the PR with copy + a11y notes and a screenshot for the change log. thanks! :thumbsup:
